anchors.window_covered: Before the US open on Thursday 27 August 2026 (Q2 FY26 earnings)

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied 10.5% is modestly rich versus 8.97% mean / 7.39% median realised abs move; central case ±6-8% with upward skew. A Q2 beat is priced; the FY-guide reaction is the real question -- options pay for the guide, not the quarter.
key_drivers: Bar is a beat-and-raise, not a beat: consensus sits inside the guide and is unchanged over 30 days (ESP 0.00%); the FY26 adj-EPS guide is the only number that matters

The metric this quarter is traffic, not EPS -- Q1 comps were ticket-only (traffic -1.0%); third-party foot-traffic shows Q2 rolling traffic +1.4%, July +4.5% (best in nine quarters), which is why Jefferies lifted Q2 comps to 3.4%
Margin/FCF stack intact and the tariff assumption looks conservative -- guidance assumes tariffs step back up in H2 and excludes any IEEPA refunds, both unbooked optionality
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The stock is the problem, not the P&L -- it has run ~35% in three months against a Hold consensus and an average target below spot; an in-line raise after last quarter's +17.9% gap gives back 6-10% on perfectly good numbers, and Dollar General reporting the same morning can set a negative cohort tone first.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: FY26 adjusted-EPS consensus could not be cleanly resolved between two conflicting reads ($6.72 vs implied ~$7.17); left unresolved rather than picking one.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Front weekly prices ~10.0-10.5%, rich versus median abs 7.39%/mean abs 8.97% -- only 2 of the last 8 reactions exceeded 10.5%. Centre is +/-6-8% realised; treat 10.5% as ~1SD, not a cap -- the -22% tail is real.
key_drivers: Puts are the crowded side: front weekly call/put ~1:1.7, 50-day put/call volume ratio at the 86th percentile -- hedges to unwind on an in-line print
Short base modest but real: 5.18% of float, 3.41 days to cover -- enough for a de-risking pop, not a true squeeze
Spot sits above the median and average sell-side target with the run-up already having happened, capping the upside asymmetry a put-heavy book would otherwise create
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: Bar is high and chart extended -- a merely reiterated guide is a sell-the-news event into a stock 14.6% above its 200DMA; DLTR's worst historical reactions were all guidance resets, and August is the stock's historically worst month.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source IV rank/percentile, term structure, borrow fee, strike-level OI concentration, or dealer gamma.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Options price ~10.5% vs median realised 7.4%/mean 9.0% -- realised likely lands 7-9%; the good news (traffic inflection, likely raise) is already the consensus script, so the magnitude is over-priced more than the direction.
key_drivers: Real demand signal already public: Placer.ai July same-store visits +4.8% YoY, syndicated across trade press and cited by sell-side before the print -- genuine but fully priced
Sell-side capitulation is complete: Goldman dropped its Sell, multiple upgrades, yet spot trades ABOVE the average target -- no one left to convert
Retail is not the crowded side (Stocktwits reads Neutral, unremarkable volume); the two-session fade from $140 to $133 on below-average volume looks like fast money de-risking into the event
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The demand data is real and the bar is low against a 32% average surprise; a beat-and-raise on a confirmed traffic inflection is exactly the setup that produced +17.9% last quarter, with some longs already shaken out by the recent fade.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: No Stocktwits time series, Reddit thread volume, short interest, or options skew directly sourced; crowding read leans on analyst-tone shift and tape.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Expect ~7-8% absolute vs 10.51% implied -- the straddle looks rich. 20-print mean abs 8.7%/median 8.1%, only 30% exceeded 10.5%. Direction close to a coin flip but magnitude distribution is left-skewed (median up +3.6% vs down -10.0%), so EV tilt is negative even at 50/50 odds.
key_drivers: 20-quarter sample: 9 up/11 down (45% up) with persistent negative magnitude skew -- no directional edge with bad tail asymmetry
Structural break: only 4 post-Family-Dollar-divestiture prints exist (3 up/1 down, mean +4.9%) -- too thin (n=4) to overturn the 20-quarter rate

Setup cohort is the negative input: spot near the top of its 52-week range, ~40% off April lows, above the mean analyst target -- the classic run-up-into-an-expensive-print cohort that historically converts beats into flat-to-lower tape
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The regime that matters may be the 4-quarter pure-play one, not the 20-quarter conglomerate one -- post-divestiture DLTR has beaten and raised three prints running, analysts are still catching up, and a $2.5B buyback gives an underweighted book fuel to squeeze higher even on a mediocre print.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source per-quarter T+1 to T+5 drift returns or a matched sector/size/IV cohort study; break-rate computed against today's implied rather than each quarter's own implied.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Expect a realised move of roughly 6-8%, below the 10.51% implied and closer to the 7.4% median -- the -22% tail that justifies 10.5% was a Family-Dollar-era event that no longer applies to a post-divestiture, single-banner Dollar Tree. Magnitude is the more mispriced variable.
key_drivers: Peer regime is bifurcated: tariff-refund-flattered beats with decelerating comps got sold (Walmart -9%, Target slipped) while traffic-led beats were rewarded (Ross +8%) -- DLTR's likely beat is traffic-led, the rewarded bucket
Third-party data reads through directly: Jefferies cited Placer rolling traffic +1.4% in Q2 vs -0.8% in Q1, strongest in nine quarters, and lifted its own Q2 comp estimate above the guide midpoint
Cross-asset backdrop cuts both ways: elevated gasoline/core PCE pressures the discretionary basket but is also a trade-down accelerant into $1.25-$7 formats
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: DLTR could print a tariff-refund-flattered beat and get treated like Walmart (-9% on a beat-and-raise) if the underlying comp only meets guidance; same-day Dollar General caution would compound it mechanically.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source a DLTR-specific IEEPA tariff-refund quantification, short interest, options skew, or ETF/index flow figure.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Model a realised absolute move of ~7-9% vs the 10.5% implied -- modestly rich but not egregiously so, since the IEEPA tariff-refund disclosure is a genuine fat-tail on both sides this quarter. Direction close to a coin flip; size is not.
panel_verdicts.strongest_reversal_case: The bar is already at the top of the company's own range with no valuation cushion -- consensus sits at the top of the $1.00-1.15 guide while the average sell-side target sits below spot with a Hold consensus. Q1 comps were ticket-led with traffic down 1.0%, and the ticket engine (tariff-driven pricing) structurally rolls off now that IEEPA tariffs were struck down; add Mantle Ridge's exit removing the activist bid and DLTR's historically weak August seasonality, and a cautious Q3/H2 frame on a headline beat is the single most likely path to a -10% print.
panel_verdicts.what_would_break_my_reversal_case: A quantified, sizeable IEEPA refund recognised in the quarter alongside an FY26 EPS raise above $7.10 and positive traffic comps -- simultaneously killing the ticket-only critique and forcing target upgrades from a sell-side currently below spot.
key_drivers: Bar set at the top of guidance after a 32.1% average four-quarter surprise -- the whisper is higher than the tape
Comp quality: Q1 traffic -1.0% with all growth from ticket; post-SCOTUS tariff removal undermines the pricing engine that drove it
No valuation cushion (18.6x forward, avg PT below spot) vs offsets: ~9.8% short interest, a replenished $2.5B buyback, and a de-risking slide into the print
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: Q2 is mechanically the first quarter of lower landed cost, and if DLTR also recognises a large excluded tariff refund the margin beat could be large enough that guidance conservatism is ignored -- a 10%+ squeeze against a ~9.8% short base is entirely live.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source a true buy-side whisper number, Q2 traffic/ticket split, DLTR-specific IEEPA refund amount, or current borrow cost.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Expect ~6-8% realised versus the 10.51% implied. Implied sits above both mean-abs (8.97%) and median-abs (7.39%); the two genuine tail events (-22.2%, +17.9%) came from a period of CEO/CFO churn and the Family Dollar overhang that no longer exists. Direction close to a coin flip; size is the mispricing.
key_drivers: No informative insider signal: zero purchases in 12 months, only tax-withholding RSU-vest sales; the one large print (Mantle Ridge/Hilal, ~$248M) is a fund wind-down/distribution mechanic, not a view on Q2 -- and Hilal stayed on the board

Communication signal is confidence rising, not falling: Q1 was a guide raise with disclosure tightening (explicitly excluding tariff refunds), and the board replenished the buyback to $2.5B right after the company itself bought stock at $111
Alt-data (Placer.ai traffic +1.4% in Q2, +4.5% in July) corroborates a comp beat but is already public -- Jefferies published the same read on 8/19, so the edge is arbitraged into the price
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: Sell-the-news on a good print -- if DLTR delivers near the top of guidance but merely reaffirms rather than raises again, a stock that has run 20% off June lows and sits above two-thirds of sell-side targets gives back 8-10% on objectively fine numbers.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source current-cycle short interest (best figure ~9.8% of float, stale from Jan-2026), 10b5-1 plan disclosures, or live options-flow/dark-pool prints.

synthesis.move_band_note: unsigned magnitude band, right-skewed; the implied move is roughly one standard deviation, not a cap
synthesis.early_prediction: No directional edge: consensus +5.4, with no persona scoring beyond |18| in either direction -- Fundamental (+18) and Options & Positioning (+14) lean on a traffic-led comp beat and a put-heavy, de-risked options book, while Sentiment (-11) and Base-Rates (-8) lean on a rich implied move and an expensive setup cohort into a stock trading above its average price target. Main driver: whether the Q2 beat is traffic-led (rewarded, per Ross) or tariff-refund-flattered with a decelerating core comp (punished, per Walmart) -- the two outcomes this cycle's retail tape has treated very differently. Main caveat: implied move (10.51%) is rich versus realised history (8.97% mean / 7.39% median), so even a correct direction call risks overstating the size, and reversal risk sits at Med-High (59.7 consensus, red-team 60) on a name whose worst historical prints were guidance resets.
synthesis.red_team_survival_note: The red-team case (the bar already sits at the top of guidance, Q1 comps were ticket-only with traffic down 1.0%, and the tariff-driven pricing engine structurally rolls off now that IEEPA tariffs were struck down) is specific and sourced, and it converges with Sentiment's and Base-Rates' independent bearish reads on the same over-priced-setup logic. It does not overturn the panel: Fundamental and Options & Positioning independently found the opposite from cited third-party foot-traffic data (Placer.ai, Jefferies) showing a genuine traffic inflection distinct from Q1's ticket-only comp -- a real fact the red-team case does not dispute, it only argues the market already knows it. The panel nets to a genuine coin flip on direction with real disagreement on both sides, not a suppressed lean.
synthesis.chair_independence_note: Four of seven personas (Fundamental, Sentiment, Macro/Peers, Forensics) independently found and cited the same Placer.ai/Jefferies foot-traffic datapoint (Q2 rolling traffic +1.4%, July +4.5%) as central evidence, though they split on whether it is already fully priced (Sentiment, Forensics) or still underappreciated (Fundamental, Macro/Peers) -- convergence on the single most visible alt-data point for this name, not independent corroboration of the same conclusion. Reversal risk is not adjusted further for this beyond what the formula already applies, since the directional readings drawn from the shared fact genuinely diverged.
